paths.description: Homepage: primary live scores/news hub and global navigation; tested desktop, mobile, preferences, performance, privacy and memory.
Representative news article: content/detail template and crawler/no-JS visibility.
Representative match detail: live/result data template on a narrow mobile viewport.
Representative competition/listing template with standings/news navigation.
Invalid URL: HTTP/error recovery and route continuity.

findings.summary: The site remains light under a dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-condition screenshot is visually identical to the light capture, the computed root colorScheme is normal, and static CSS inspection found no prefers-color-scheme rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven dark surface/text tokens using prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Continuous animations remain active when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe matched the preference but reported 171 animations, including pulse and repeated 1s openweb animations still running.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable non-essential animation and auto-motion inside prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

findings.summary: High-contrast preference produces no visible adaptation.
findings.evidence: The prefers-contrast: more screenshot is pixel-equivalent in appearance to the default capture; static inspection found no forced-colors support.
findings.suggestedFix: Add tested prefers-contrast/forced-colors adaptations and retain system colors for essential controls.

findings.summary: A consent wall obscures the entire primary experience on every tested template.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots of home, article, match and competition all show a large modal before content can be used; mobile CTA text is clipped at the edge.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, non-blocking consent control with equally prominent accept/reject choices and an accessible preference dialog.

findings.summary: Long pages do not expose scroll-aware orientation or progress.
findings.evidence: The homepage is 22,760 CSS px tall; static inspection found no scroll-state rules and screenshots show static chrome with no article/page progress cue.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight scroll progress/orientation cue using scroll-state container queries or a declarative progress pattern.

findings.summary: The consent modal is implemented as a fixed div rather than a native dialog.
findings.evidence: The quality probe found a large fixed DIV with role=dialog and aria-modal=true, while the DOM probe found zero dialog, popover and details elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Use <dialog> with a labelled heading and explicit close/reject controls, preserving focus and Escape behavior.

findings.summary: Advertising and consent chrome dominate the initial viewport.
findings.evidence: All representative screenshots reserve a large top ad slot and then cover the remaining content with consent UI, leaving little immediately usable content.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer non-essential ad chrome, reserve compact slots, and keep the primary score/news content dominant.

findings.summary: Numerous controls are too small for reliable touch interaction.
findings.evidence: The active probe counted 17 controls below 24 px in one dimension; Lighthouse target-size failed 12 elements, although keyboard focus itself was visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase interactive hit areas to at least 24 by 24 CSS px, preferably 44 px for primary mobile controls, without relying on hover.

findings.summary: Cold-load performance and stability are far outside good ranges.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 18.1s, CLS 0.645, TBT 2,820ms and Time to Interactive 41.3s, producing performance score 0.09.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP asset, reserve all late content space, cut main-thread work, and defer non-critical third parties.

findings.summary: The page shifts substantially during the measured load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured CLS 0.645; image inspection found 85 of 100 images without explicit dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Set width/height or aspect-ratio for media and reserve deterministic space for ads, scores, and consent UI.

findings.summary: Long JavaScript tasks block interaction.
findings.evidence: The trace recorded 5 long tasks, a 379.68ms longest task and 508.84ms TBT; Lighthouse measured 2,820ms TBT under throttling.
findings.suggestedFix: Break up long tasks, delay analytics/comments/ads, and schedule non-visible work at lower priority.

findings.summary: The initial page makes an excessive network request set.
findings.evidence: HAR captured 551 requests and 3.97MB transferred, including 88 scripts totaling 2.84MB and 156 fetch/XHR requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Shorten critical chains, cache first-party assets, and lazy-load comments, analytics and advertising only when needed.

findings.summary: Large amounts of shipped JavaScript and CSS are unused.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 1,994KiB unused JavaScript and 115KiB unused CSS; HAR recorded 88 script requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split by route and feature, remove duplicate/legacy bundles, and conditionally import ad/comment integrations.

findings.summary: Interactive controls lack accessible names and valid ARIA.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found 14 unnamed buttons, 5 unnamed links, one prohibited ARIA use, one unlabeled select and an untitled iframe.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every control and frame a programmatic name, pair selects with labels, and remove prohibited ARIA.

findings.summary: Many text/control combinations fail minimum contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse color-contrast audit failed 189 nodes.
findings.suggestedFix: Update foreground/background tokens to meet WCAG AA in default and preference modes.

findings.summary: The homepage lacks a primary H1 and includes unnamed focusable links.
findings.evidence: Rendered homepage probe found zero H1 elements and the focusable list begins with an anchor with no text or aria-label; Lighthouse found unnamed links.
findings.suggestedFix: Add one descriptive H1 and ensure every focus stop has a discernible name while retaining the visible focus ring.

findings.summary: Viewport settings restrict zoom and targets are undersized.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports maximum-scale below 5 or user-scalable=no plus 12 insufficient target-size failures.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove zoom restrictions and enlarge/space mobile controls; keep the successful no-horizontal-overflow behavior.

findings.summary: The page logs browser errors during load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse errors-in-console failed with 9 table entries.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix uncaught/network integration errors and gate optional third-party failures so they do not pollute the main page runtime.

findings.summary: Most images lack intrinsic dimensions.
findings.evidence: Image inspection found 85 of 100 images without width/height and 97 legacy-format URLs; Lighthouse unsized-images only partially passed.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit intrinsic dimensions/aspect ratios and responsive modern sources from the image pipeline.

findings.summary: The page has deprecation, BFCache, source-map and DevTools issues.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found one deprecated API, two BFCache blockers, 10 missing source maps for large first-party scripts, and one inspector issue.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove deprecated APIs and unload blockers, publish production source maps securely, and resolve DevTools issues.

findings.summary: Many links are not crawlable anchors.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse crawlable-anchors failed 97 items, despite the page having a valid viewport and robots.txt.
findings.suggestedFix: Use real <a href> navigation for routes and descriptive link text; reserve buttons for in-page actions.

findings.summary: Transport policy and cookie attributes are weaker than the HTTPS origin suggests.
findings.evidence: Headers probe found no HSTS and CSP allows unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval; cookies probe found three non-Secure cookies and every observed cookie had SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Add HSTS, migrate CSP to nonces/hashes without unsafe-eval, and set Secure plus the narrowest appropriate SameSite policy.

findings.summary: The page contacts an extreme number of third parties and trackers.
findings.evidence: Tracker capture saw 48 third-party origins and seven known tracker domains; Spot.IM alone made 337 requests across two origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit and remove vendors, delay all non-essential trackers until valid consent, and batch/minimise analytics.

findings.summary: Browser defenses are incomplete.
findings.evidence: HSTS is missing and CSP permits unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval; clickjacking, nosniff, referrer and permissions policies are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy HSTS and a nonce/hash CSP, then evaluate Trusted Types for the script-heavy Next.js application.

findings.summary: Consent presents acceptance more prominently than refusal.
findings.evidence: The blocking modal has a bright accept button but no equally prominent reject action; the alternative is a smaller cookie-customisation text link.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer reject-all beside accept-all with equal visual weight, concise purposes, and reversible preferences.

findings.summary: The image pipeline rarely provides responsive modern assets.
findings.evidence: Image inspection found 97 legacy-format URLs, 85 missing dimensions, two oversized images and two missing srcset opportunities.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP variants, responsive srcset/sizes and intrinsic dimensions; preserve SVG where appropriate.

findings.summary: Background integrations perform hundreds of requests before user intent.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 551 requests while tracker evidence shows 201 API and 136 pixel requests to Spot.IM during initial load.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not initialize comments/ads below the fold until proximity or interaction; batch events and deprioritize background fetches.

findings.summary: Third-party script cost is disproportionate to the core score/news task.
findings.evidence: The page loads 48 third-party origins, 88 scripts and 2.84MB of script transfer before the user engages with optional features.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party budget, remove low-value vendors, and lazy-load remaining media/comment/ad code.

taskList.title: Cut the load path and defer third-party ads/comments/analytics
Replace the blocking, asymmetric consent wall
Repair accessible names, contrast, zoom and target sizing
Reserve media/ad space and modernize responsive images
Harden CSP, HSTS and cookie attributes
Add dark, reduced-motion and high-contrast preference support
Make all navigation links crawlable and clear runtime hygiene issues
